version.changelog: Initial release: Create and configure new OpenClaw agents with workspace structure, memory system, and Feishu bindings

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: create-agent-feishu
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides legitimate instructions and templates for an AI agent to automate the creation and configuration of new OpenClaw agents, specifically focusing on Feishu integration. It includes standard administrative tasks such as directory creation, file writing, and service restarts (SKILL.md), all of which are directly aligned with its stated purpose of agent management without any signs of malicious intent or data exfiltration.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions match its stated purpose (creating an OpenClaw agent and configuring Feishu bindings); nothing requested or installed is disproportionate, but pay attention to how and where Feishu secrets are stored and to the example's use of /root paths.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (create an OpenClaw agent, workspace, memory files, openclaw.json edits, and Feishu channel bindings) match the SKILL.md instructions. Required actions (create workspace files, edit openclaw.json, add Feishu appId/appSecret, add bindings) are exactly what you'd expect for this feature.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are explicit about creating directories and writing persona/memory files and about editing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and bindings. They do not instruct reading unrelated host data or exfiltrating information. Two points to watch: the examples use absolute /root/.openclaw paths (inconsistent with earlier ~/.openclaw usage) which implies running as root; and the doc tells the user to place Feishu appSecret values into openclaw.json (sensitive data stored on disk).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only with no install spec and no packaged code — lowest risk from an installation perspective (nothing is downloaded or written by the skill itself).
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not declare required env vars or request unrelated credentials. It does instruct the operator to add Feishu AppID/AppSecret to the OpenClaw config, which is proportionate to providing Feishu integration but means sensitive secrets will be stored in a config file — the operator should ensure secure storage and file permissions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not modify other skills' configs, and is user-invocable. It does require filesystem access to the OpenClaw home/config, which is expected for this task.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says, but take these practical precautions before using it: 1) Protect Feishu secrets: appSecret/appId are sensitive—store them only in the intended OpenClaw config and set file permissions to restrict access (e.g., chmod 600). 2) Prefer your real user home over /root: the examples sometimes use /root/.openclaw; run commands as the intended agent user (replace /root with your $HOME) to avoid running as root. 3) Review openclaw.json before and after edits and keep backups; verify agent IDs are unique to avoid accidental routing. 4) Limit exposures: use allowFrom/allowlist policies where appropriate so bots aren't open to everyone. 5) Test in an isolated environment first if possible, and rotate credentials if they were accidentally exposed. 6) If you need the skill to run automatically or to store secrets elsewhere (env vault), plan for secure secret management — the SKILL.md currently assumes storing secrets in the config file.
